about: CMB against global PC read at the target on its paper's Alarm setting, every node a target; the release summary's CMB entry is built from it
build: Andrey pre-release build of 13 November 2026 (the 0.18.0 release branch as merged with LOAD's skeleton step); the release branch of 14 November 2026, with exact upper-tail p-values, gave the same answers and test counts at every target of the 3 datasets rerun
hardware: AMD EPYC 7713 64-Core Processor, 1 core per fit, 1 BLAS thread; CMB, Andrey's PC, and bnlearn ran in the same run, one fit after the other, on shared nodes, so the times are indicative
verdict_rule: no reference implementation exists, so each row sets Andrey's means beside the paper's (Table 1) and judges CMB against two global PCs read at the target, Andrey's pc with the same test and level and bnlearn 5.2.1 pc.stable with mi-adf: the mean over paired datasets of CMB's total minus the other's with its 95% percentile-bootstrap interval, better or worse when the interval lies wholly on that side of 0 over at least 10 datasets, on seeds 0-19, and a cell worse there counts only when it is worse again on seeds 20-39. The floor: per dataset, the total minus the empty answer's; a row passes when its interval lies wholly below 0
error_metric: total: per target, the edges at the target missing or extra against the true CPDAG plus those whose direction differs from it, an edge the CPDAG directs and the answer leaves undirected included (reversed); a dataset's value is the mean over its targets. lenient leaves out the undirected ones. The floor uses the total against the empty answer's, the target's degree
fit_protocol: each fit in a fresh process on one core with one BLAS thread, CMB once per target and each PC once per dataset, read at every target; no warm-up, a cap of 1,800 s per fit, past which a fit is a timeout and never scored; no fit failed or timed out. G-square tests at alpha 0.02 with no limit on the conditioning set, CMB with HITON-MB, its default blanket learner
seeds_note: every cell holds 20 datasets, seeds 0-19, and 20 fresh datasets, seeds 20-39
cells_note: net:alarm:1000: forward samples of the Alarm network's own tables, the columns in an order drawn from the seed; every answer is scored at each target against the CPDAG
